newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico City's second airport sees shaky future.
newsitem.headline: Mexico City's second airport sees shaky future.

text.p: The clock is ticking toward the end of the decade, when the airport in one of the world's biggest cities, Mexico City, is expected to outgrow its current site and be replaced.
The project has been talked about here for years -- so many years in fact, that the current airport has been rebuilding to improve facilities even though everyone knows it will be superseded soon.
But the Mexican government now says the long-delayed new Mexico City airport should take one step closer to construction in coming weeks, after a year of intense debate over rival sites.
Before the year's end, the Communications and Transportation Ministry hopes to decide which of two finalist sites in states neighboring the capital will harbour the airport.

Private companies have been told bidding for the contract to construct and operate the new Mexico City airport will begin in the first two months of next year. Construction may not begin until 1998, with completion scheduled for 2000.

The capital's Benito Juarez airport has just two runways, built too close to each other to allow simultaneous take-offs and landings. Expansion would now be impossible because of surrounding residential areas, said a ministry spokesman.
Increasing traffic means Benito Juarez will be outgrown by 2002, he added.
Mexico City's airport expects to see between 16 and 18 million passengers this year, but the figure is projected to increase to 25.4 million travellers per year by 2000.
Although the site is spatially inadequate, the difficulty of replacing Benito Juarez means it is likely to be phased out gradually rather than replaced outright, the ministry said.

For now, the airport is being expanded, with a new hotel in the works and a new international terminal just finished. A total $110 million will be spent on the overhaul, according to contracted constructors Grupo Hakim.
The government declines to guess how much the new airport would cost, saying it will be paid for by the private sector, which will recoup the cost through levies on travellers.
Local newspapers have reported an estimated $30 billion could be necessary to build the airport, its runways and transport linking it to the capital.

Complicating plans for the new airport is a national project to privatize the country's 57 airports, selling off operating rights to domestic and foreign companies by the end of 1997, the ministry official said.
In addition, while government officials say the new terminal would initially complement Benito Juarez, Mexican airline directors want to keep flights at one site.

"The two directors (of Mexicana de Aviacion and Aerovias de Mexico) are both in favor of a single airport, as cities with two airports have proven to have difficulty with connections," said Fernando Martinez, spokesman for Mexico's two airlines, represented by the company Cintra.
Foreign airline directors are worried their costly investments in terminal facilities, routing and ticketing at the Benito Juarez airport could go to waste.
"United Airlines has a strong investment here in the Benito Juarez airport over many years and we are very comfortable here," airline director general Josue Meza said.
"We want to know and have been assured that our investments will not be for nothing," he added.
American Airlines, for one, said it spent $11 million to set up its terminal operations at Benito Juarez.
"We are waiting just like everyone else," airline director general Enrique Cruz said, referring to future plans in Mexico City regarding the new airport.

Of the two front-runner sites for the new terminal, one lies in Tizayuca in the state of Hidalgo, about 40 miles (70 km) to the northeast of Mexico City, while the other is Texcoco in the State of Mexico, a shorter 20-mile (30 km) ride from the center of the nation's capital.
Also being considered in the site selection is available space for runways. Tizayuca has room for four runways, while Texcoco has space for just two.
